subject: social_science

concepts.title: Lineage and Ancestry of the Mughals
concepts.definition: The ruling Mughal family possessed dual royal heritage, tracing maternal roots to Genghis Khan of the Mongols and paternal ties to Timur of Central Asia.
concepts.key_idea: Mughals proudly identified with Timurid heritage while disassociating from Mongol massacres.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history who were the ancestors of the Mughals
describe the dual lineage of Mughal rulers
why did Mughals prefer Timurid ancestry over Mongol ancestry
explain how Genghis Khan and Timur were related to the Mughals
identify the paternal and maternal roots of the Mughal dynasty

solution_steps.explain: Trace lineage from Genghis Khan who ruled parts of China and Central Asia.
Trace lineage from Timur who ruled Iran, Iraq, and modern Turkey.
Note that Genghis Khan was linked to memory of massacres and Uzbeg rivals.

concepts.title: Mughal Inheritance Practices
concepts.definition: Rather than following eldest-son inheritance, the Mughals practiced shared family succession where royal territories were split among all imperial sons.
concepts.key_idea: Division of royal estates equally among sons instead of reserving full rights for the eldest son.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history compare primogeniture and coparcenary inheritance
what tradition of succession was followed by Mughal emperors
explain why Mughals divided their inheritance among all sons
differentiate between coparcenary division and eldest son inheritance
how did Mughal succession rules differ from primogeniture

solution_steps.explain: Inheritance model where only the eldest son receives the complete paternal estate.
Mughal and Timurid custom of partitioning inheritance among all sons.

concepts.title: Mughal Relations with Rajputs and Regional Rulers
concepts.definition: Mughal imperial expansion relied on a combination of military operations and marital alliances with local rulers, ensuring respectful treatment even after battlefield victories.
concepts.key_idea: Strategic integration of vanquished and voluntary regional rulers through high posts and land assignments.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history how did Mughals deal with defeated rulers
describe Mughal relations with Rajput rulers
explain the diplomatic balance maintained by Mughals toward regional chiefs
what policy did Mughals adopt after conquering opposing rulers
discuss how marriage alliances strengthened Mughal power

solution_steps.explain: Observe marriages with Rajput families such as Amber and Marwar princesses.
Recognize that defeated adversaries were honourably given back their lands as assignments.

concepts.title: Mansabdari System and Administration
concepts.definition: The Mughal administrative framework assigned ranked positions to military and civil officers, determining their pay, required cavalry contingent, and land revenue allocations.
concepts.key_idea: Hierarchical grading mechanism linking salary and cavalry obligations to numerical rank values.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history define mansabdar and explain the role of zat
what were the responsibilities of a mansabdar in Mughal administration
how was the salary and status of a mansabdar fixed
explain the difference between mansabdar and jagirdar
describe how sawars were inspected and maintained by a noble

solution_steps.explain: Mansab refers to a rank or position held by an individual officer in Mughal service.
Zat determined prestige, salary, and position in the imperial court.

solution_steps.action: Identify sawar duties and jagir assignments
solution_steps.explain: Nobles maintained cavalrymen (sawars) and received salaries through revenue assignments called jagirs.

concepts.title: Percentage of High Ranking Mansabdars
concepts.definition: Evaluating the numerical proportion of top-tier imperial officers relative to the entire military and civil administration.
concepts.key_idea: Mathematical calculation of the concentration of high-ranking nobles in the Mughal state hierarchy.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history compute the percentage of high ranking mansabdars given high_rank_count and total_mansabdars
calculate the percentage share of top mansabdars in Mughal service
find what percentage of total mansabdars held high ranks in Akbar or Shah Jahan administration
determine the proportion of high rank nobles out of total mansabdars
what is the percentage of high ranking mansabdars if high_rank_count is high_rank_count and total_mansabdars is total_mansabdars

solution_steps.action: Calculate ratio of high ranking mansabdars
solution_steps.explain: Divide high rank count by total mansabdars
Multiply ratio by 100

concepts.title: Zabt Revenue System and Zamindars
concepts.definition: A structured land revenue arrangement introduced by Todar Mal, relying on extensive crop yields and price surveys across individual revenue districts.
concepts.key_idea: Tax collection based on decade-long statistical assessment of agricultural productivity and land surveys.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history what was the zabt revenue system
explain the role of Todar Mal in Mughal land revenue collection
who were zamindars and what was their role in Mughal administration
describe how revenue rates were fixed for individual crops under zabt
why was zabt not applicable in regions like Bengal and Gujarat

solution_steps.explain: Akbar revenue minister conducted a 10-year survey of crop yields, prices, and cultivated areas.
Each province had revenue circles with fixed schedule rates for individual crops.
Zamindars were local headmen or chieftains acting as tax collecting intermediaries.

concepts.title: Akbar Nama and Ain-i Akbari
concepts.definition: A comprehensive three-part historical documentation authored by Abul Fazl detailing Akbar's lineage, administrative events, and statistical records of the empire.
concepts.key_idea: Detailed chronicle containing administrative facts, economic figures, and cultural details of Akbar's empire.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history what is the significance of Akbar Nama and Ain-i Akbari
who wrote Akbar Nama and what contents are covered in its three volumes
explain the statistical importance of Ain-i Akbari
describe the historical work composed by Abul Fazl for Akbar
what information does the third volume of Akbar Nama provide

solution_steps.explain: Abul Fazl wrote a three-volume history of Akbar reign titled Akbar Nama.
Ain-i Akbari contains administrative details, crop yields, prices, wages, and revenue statistics.

concepts.title: Sulh-i Kul and Akbar's Governance Policy
concepts.definition: An inclusive governance philosophy of universal harmony championed by Akbar, advocating tolerance, justice, and non-discrimination across religious beliefs.
concepts.key_idea: Statecraft built on broad religious tolerance, ethical administration, and peaceful coexistence.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history explain Akbar policy of sulh-i kul
what does the term sulh-i kul mean and how was it implemented
describe how debates at Ibadat Khana influenced Akbar ideas of governance
how did Jahangir describe the concept of universal peace followed by his father
why was universal tolerance important for governing a diverse Mughal empire

solution_steps.explain: Sulh-i kul translates to universal peace, prohibiting discrimination based on religion or creed.
System focused on honesty, justice, and peace enforced uniformly across the imperial state.

concepts.title: Mansabdar Rank Increase Calculation
concepts.definition: Determining the total expansion in high-ranking noble numbers across successive Mughal rulers' reigns.
concepts.key_idea: Measuring the administrative growth of mansabdar appointments over time.
question_patterns: in Class 7 history find the increase in 5000 zat mansabdars from Akbar reign to Aurangzeb reign
calculate the net increase in mansabdars between two periods
determine how many more mansabdars were present given count_aurangzeb and count_akbar
what is the total increase in top rank mansabdars from count_akbar to count_aurangzeb
compute the growth in mansabdar count given count_akbar and count_aurangzeb

solution_steps.action: Subtract Akbar era mansabdar count from Aurangzeb era count
solution_steps.explain: Find the difference between final and initial mansabdar counts
